author: Sunshine Sentinel
title: Sarasota Art Museum to offer free summer admission for military families
text:
Sarasota Art Museum of Ringling College of Art and Design announced on Apr. 29 that it will participate in the Blue Star Museums program, offering free admission to currently serving U.S. military personnel and their families from May 16 through September 7, 2026.
The initiative aims to provide military families with access to cultural experiences during the summer months. The Blue Star Museums program is a partnership between the National Endowment for the Arts and Blue Star Families, in collaboration with the Department of Defense and museums nationwide.
Military visitors at Sarasota Art Museum this summer will have complimentary access to three exhibitions: Something Borrowed, Something New; Maria A. Guzmán Capron: Penumbra; and Beautiful Ideas: The Prints of Sol LeWitt. Virginia Shearer, executive director of Sarasota Art Museum, said, “It’s especially fitting that our exhibition, Beautiful Ideas: The Prints of Sol LeWitt, coincides with this year’s Blue Star Museums program. Sol LeWitt, himself, was a Veteran. He served in the U.S. Army for two years—from 1951to1953—during the Korean War, working primarily as a graphic artist and designing recruitment posters. This connection makes the program all the more personal and meaningful.”
Mary Anne Carter, Senior Advisor for the National Endowment for the Arts said, “The National Endowment for the Arts is honored to help connect military service members and their families with their communities through the Blue Star Museums program. Institutions like Sarasota Art Museum of Ringling College of Art and Design offer opportunities for military members to create special memories and connect with our country’s heritage and culture.” Kathy Roth-Douquet, CEO of Blue Star Families added: “For 15 years, Blue Star Museums has opened doors for military families to explore, connect, and feel at home in their communities…Museums are more than cultural spaces—they’re places where military families feel seen, welcomed, and celebrated.”
In addition to its exhibitions space totaling 15,000 square feet along with an auditorium and outdoor sculpture garden according to its official website, Sarasota Art Museum promotes diversity by building a community that values varied perspectives through art according to its official website. Amenities include a bistro shop as well as an outdoor sculpture garden according to its official website. The museum collaborates closely with Ringling College as a platform for education in contemporary art according to its official website.
The museum also works toward promoting understanding of contemporary art via exhibitions encouraging visual thinking and ethical awareness according to its official website. Shearer has served as executive director at Sarasota Art Museum according to its official website.
Participation in programs like Blue Star Museums highlights efforts by institutions such as Sarasota Art Museum not only toward accessibility but also fostering connections between diverse communities.
